one_liner: Amazon's cloud-only REST API for sellers and vendors (Selling Partner API).

auth.notes: A third party acting for a selling partner uses Login with Amazon. The partner authorizes the app, and the integration exchanges the refresh token for a short-lived access token whose token type is bearer. Grantless calls use the OAuth client-credentials grant with the same client id and secret. There is no separate static API key or personal access token.

access.notes: Anyone with Amazon credentials can open a Solution Provider Portal account and register a sandbox application while the developer profile is still under review, and that sandbox can make test calls immediately. Amazon then evaluates the profile and decides whether to grant or deny Selling Partner API access, and it may ask for more information. Private seller applications also require a Professional selling account. Individual accounts are not eligible. Public apps must be listed in the Selling Partner Appstore. There is no paid API plan or sales contract.

api.notes: SP-API is a public REST API covering orders, shipments, payments, inventory, listings, pricing, and fulfillment, with read and write operations. Data Kiosk adds GraphQL queries for analytics. The reference is readable without logging in. Only Amazon's hosted sellingpartnerapi endpoints are documented, and nothing is self-hosted.

mcp.notes: Amazon Selling Partner Developer Services published Local MCP for SP-API in May 2026 as the npm package @amazon-sp-api-release/sp-api-dev-mcp. It ships two servers that are configurable and usable now in MCP clients. Community servers also exist, including jay-trivedi's amazon_sp_mcp and DataDoe's hosted endpoint, but the vendor server is the one reported here.

verdict.rationale: The public REST API is broad and documented, and a sandbox app can be registered and called while review is pending. Amazon must approve the developer profile before SP-API access is granted, and private seller development also requires a Professional selling account.

evidence.quote: A Login with Amazon (LWA) <<glossary:access token>> authorizes your application to take certain actions on behalf of a <<glossary:selling partner>>.
An LWA access token expires one hour after it is issued.
For more information, visit the Authorization Code Grant page in the Login with Amazon documentation.
This sandbox application lets you start testing API calls immediately, even while your developer profile is under review.

The decision to grant or deny Selling Partner API access is made based on the information that you provide in your Developer Profile, including but not limited to your application functionality and your compliance with the Acceptable Use Policy and the Data Protection Policy.
Note that in Seller Central, you must have a professional selling account to develop SP-API private seller applications.
The Selling Partner API (SP-API) is a REST-based API that helps sellers and vendors access their data on orders, shipments, payments, inventory, and other business information.
The API supports building applications that automate Amazon business operations.
You use the Data Kiosk API to submit <<glossary:GraphQL>> queries for data from a variety of schemas to help selling partners manage their businesses.
Local MCP for SP-API brings this to the SP-API ecosystem as a consolidated npm package bundling MCP servers for Amazon Selling Partner API development.

Configure it in your MCP-compatible IDE, and your AI assistant is equipped with authoritative SP-API knowledge, actionable developer tools for code generation, optimization, and migration, and a workflow engine to build and execute multi-step API operations.
Authored by: Tong S. Solutions Architect, Selling Partner Developer Services
Amazon is an e-commerce giant delivering a massive online marketplace, cloud services, and digital products that connect retailers, consumers, and businesses worldwide for seamless transactions.
